images.filename: Flickr - Official U.S. Navy Imagery - A Sailor helps Royal Cambodian Armed Forces doctors find the right pair of glasses..jpg
images.caption: REAM, Cambodia (Oct. 23, 2011) Hospital Corpsman 1st Class Alfred Coble, assigned to Commander, Task Force 73, assists Royal Cambodian Armed Forces doctors in finding the right pair of glasses for a local man during a medical civic action project for Cooperation Afloat Readiness and Training (CARAT) Cambodia 2011. CARAT is a series of bilateral exercises held annually in Southeast Asia to strengthen relationships and enhance force readiness. (U.S. Navy photo by Lt. Cmdr. Mike Morley/Released) 111023-N-VP123-197

images.caption: U.S. Navy Master Chief Hospital Corpsman Tadeo O’Brien, center, Maritime Civil Affairs Security and Training (MCAST) command medical lead, observes and guides Royal Cambodian Armed Forces medics as they treat a simulated war injured patient in Ream, Cambodia, Oct. 25, 2012. MCAST is participating in Cooperation Afloat Readiness and Training (CARAT) Cambodia 2012. CARAT is a series of bilateral exercises held annually in Southeast Asia to strengthen relationships and enhance force readiness. (DoD photo by Chief Mass Communication Specialist Jose Lopez Jr., U.S. Navy/Released)

images.caption: U.S. Navy Cmdr. Michael Misiewicz, left, the commanding officer of the guided missile destroyer USS Mustin (DDG 89), presents a Mustin command ball cap to Cambodian navy Rear Adm. Ouk Seiha, the commander of Ream Naval Base, during Misiewic?s visit to the base in Chihanoukville, Cambodia, Dec. 2, 2010. The visit, the first for Misiewic since immigrating to the United States from Cambodia in 1973, will include bilateral training between Sailors from Mustin and members of the Royal Cambodian Armed Forces. (DoD photo by Mass Communication Specialist 3rd Class Devon Dow, U.S. Navy/Released)
